patterns.label: Dagesh Lene
patterns.explain: A dagesh lene occurs only in a BeGaD KeFaT letter (ב ג ד כ פ ת) that starts a syllable: it is preceded by silence, such as the beginning of a word, or by a silent sheva. It does not double the letter.

patterns.label: Dagesh Forte
patterns.explain: A dagesh forte doubles the letter. It can stand in any consonant except the five gutturals (א ה ח ע ר). In a BeGaD KeFaT letter it is a forte when a vowel comes before it. If the letter has a sheva under it, that sheva is vocal and the dagesh is a forte.

patterns.label: Mappiq
patterns.explain: A mappiq is not a dagesh, but it looks the same. It occurs only in a ה at the end of a word. The dot marks the ה as a consonant, not a vowel letter, so the ה is pronounced and closes the final syllable.

passages.title: Genesis 15:6–7
passages.note: Dagesh lene, dagesh forte and a mappiq in a short, well-known passage.

passages.title: Genesis 25:24–25
passages.note: The birth of Esau: three kinds of dot in two verses.

passages.title: Genesis 1:24–25
